name: cache-weather-and-pause-resume
description: Pause Claude Code and shut down, sleep or hibernate the computer once running work is done, across all sessions. Plus a band above the prompt with the prompt-cache countdown, hit rate and bar, keep-warm (on by default) that refreshes the cache before it runs out and says what that saves, context weather with the auto-compact threshold and a forecast, usage limits, a Compact button and an overview of all sessions. German and English.

language.title: Language
language.description: auto follows the locale (on Windows the system language); de or en pin it.

keepWarm.title: Keep-warm in new sessions
keepWarm.description: on: every new session starts with keep-warm checked; off: it starts unchecked. Each session's checkbox stays yours.

keepWarmHours.title: Keep-warm: hours for the 1-hour cache
keepWarmHours.description: How long keep-warm goes on in a session nobody works in, with the 1-hour cache: 1 to 18 hours (8 by default; up to 18 a refresh costs less than building the cache again, about 16 keeps it warm overnight). The 5-minute cache keeps 45 minutes.

notifications.title: Notification at the shutdown countdown
notifications.description: on: when the shutdown countdown starts, a notification through your terminal's notification channel (iTerm2, kitty, Ghostty; elsewhere at most the bell; the desktop app reports the pause itself); off: none.

shutdownMode.title: What the shutdown button does
shutdownMode.description: shutdown: shut the computer down (other programs are closed without asking on Windows); sleep: standby; hibernate: hibernation. The button and the band are named after it. Each is checked at session start; what the computer cannot do leaves the button dimmed with what is missing.

askAboveMinutes.title: Pause: ask above (minutes)
askAboveMinutes.description: When a task is likely to run longer than this many minutes at a pause, Claude asks whether to stop it now and restart it after resuming, or to let it finish.
